PainterlyNPR__AssetLibrary__Register__Me.RegisterNote: The single source of truth for the asset library's numbering: the namespace, the collections (the NN in NPR_NN_NNNN), each collection's types and the blocks of numbers they own, and the five files every asset carries. The build utility, the local server, the app and the SketchUp catalogue tool all read it; nothing else decides a number.
PainterlyNPR__AssetLibrary__Register__Me.Author: Adam Noble - Noble Architecture

PainterlyNPR__AssetLibrary__Register__Nu.NamespaceNote: Every asset Id starts NPR_: the asset namespacer, so an Id is unique beside the component library's own codes
PainterlyNPR__AssetLibrary__Register__Nu.IdPatternNote: NPR_CC_TTFI. CC the collection, 05 to 80. TT the type's block (00-99), F the family (0-9), I the item (1-9). An I of 0 is a family's base and is never an asset, as codes ending in 0 are kept for folder bases in the component library
PainterlyNPR__AssetLibrary__Register__Nu.CollectionRangeNote: Adam, 30-Oct-2026: "we will have 99 series so space them out from 05 - 80 and have before 05 and after 80 reserved"
PainterlyNPR__AssetLibrary__Register__Nu.ReservedNote: Never allocated: kept for what the library has not met yet
PainterlyNPR__AssetLibrary__Register__Nu.Spacing: 07 for vegetation (Adam's example, NPR_07_0021), every other collection on a five, so each can grow into the numbers after it
PainterlyNPR__AssetLibrary__Register__Nu.TypeBlockSizeNote: Each type owns a block of 100 numbers (07_00xx trees, 07_05xx conifers); types sit five blocks apart, so a type that outgrows its block takes the next free one
PainterlyNPR__AssetLibrary__Register__Nu.FamilySizeNote: Related assets (an oak's ages, a box ball's sizes, a lavender's habits) share a ten: 07_002x is the oak family, 07_0021 its first item. A family holds nine assets

PainterlyNPR__AssetLibrary__Register__Na.AssetFolderNote: Inside its collection's folder. The collection is the folder above, so it is not repeated: paths stay short enough for SketchUp, which cannot open a path over 259 characters
PainterlyNPR__AssetLibrary__Register__Na.SegmentNote: A segment is PascalCase; a hyphen joins words inside one (Var-01). Segments are joined by a double underscore
PainterlyNPR__AssetLibrary__Register__Na.VariantNote: Every asset carries a Var, even the first: a later variation (another age, another habit) is Var-02 in the same family
PainterlyNPR__AssetLibrary__Register__Na.MaxRelativePathNote: Characters from the library folder to the longest file. The repo sits 84 characters deep on the Vale PC, and SketchUp's Ruby cannot open a path over 259

PainterlyNPR__AssetLibrary__Register__Sl.Note: The five files of an asset, by the slot code in their names. Order is the order a catalogue lists them

Slots.Label: Data
Slots.WrittenBy: Hand, the SketchUp catalogue tool; the factory adds Geometry and Factory

Slots.Label: three.js model
Slots.Note: The base GLB proxy with its material applied, for the three.js apps: metres, +Y up, its origin at the base centre on the ground

Slots.Label: SketchUp model
Slots.WrittenBy: The SketchUp catalogue and authoring tool (next phase)
Slots.Note: The same base proxy as a SketchUp component, named like the file

Slots.Label: Proxy preview
Slots.Note: The proxy rendered in the catalogue environment: the preview for the SketchUp and three.js apps

Slots.Label: Rendered preview
Slots.Note: The asset as it is typically drawn: the standard pen and wash, in the catalogue environment

PainterlyNPR__AssetLibrary__Register__Co.Note: Code, folder, the Name used in file names, the Label a catalogue shows, and the types with their blocks. A collection with no assets yet keeps its folder (a .gitkeep) so the structure is there to grow into
